one_line: OpenAI and Microsoft released new AI models, while Nvidia reported soaring revenue amid leadership and export control shifts.

themes.title: New model releases from OpenAI and Microsoft
themes.text: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower pricing and benchmark gains, while Microsoft unveiled six new models including MAI Code 2 and Flash.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for ChatGPT Work and Codex
Microsoft unveils six AI models including MAI Code 2 and Flash
OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with benchmark gains

themes.title: Nvidia reports earnings and leadership changes
themes.text: Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in third-quarter revenue and stopped reporting Singapore unit revenue after it hit $104 billion. Meanwhile, the company faced leadership changes, export control shifts under interim CEO Colette Kress, and upcoming congressional testimony for former CEO Jensen Huang.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify before US House committees on Dec 1
Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore unit revenue in 2025 as it hit $104B
Nvidia reports Q3 revenue of $115.8B and forecasts Q4 revenue of $130B
Nvidia board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
Nvidia ends H200 chip sales in China under acting CEO Colette Kress
US Commerce Dept and DOJ investigated Megaspeed over chip exports in 2024
Nvidia board creates National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
Nvidia's startup stakes reach $65.5B as interim CEO signals caution

themes.title: U.S. tightens export rules and Chinese AI distillation
themes.text: The U.S. Commerce Department tightened export rules on AI chips to target Southeast Asian data centers providing compute to Chinese firms. Concurrently, a review showed widespread industrial use of AI distillation in China to train domestic rivals.

stories.headline: US tightens AI chip export rules, targeting Southeast Asia data centres
Review shows AI distillation moving to industrial use in China
